processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1970-01-01..1970-07-31. Source states: 'Soon afterwards cholera appeared in Lebanon, Israel, Syria, and Jordan in the Eastern Mediterranean, in the Libyan Arab Republic and Tunisia in North Africa, and in Guinea in West Africa. From Guinea, following the expected pattern the disease spread to 10 countries in West Africa and by the end of 1970 had infected Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Mali, Togo, Dahomey, Upper Volta, Nigeria and Niger.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. THE INITIAL CONDITION OF THE SEVENTH PANDEMIC IN BENIN - the first seven months of 1970, before cholera existed anywhere in West Africa. This is the earliest period in the MOSAIC window and no layer of the dataset held anything for it; the baseline's first Benin row is an annual 1970 figure of 175 cases and 37 deaths with no within-year resolution, which a weekly builder must otherwise spread across the whole year including months in which the disease had not yet reached the continent. TWO WHO SOURCES BOUND IT. (1) WER 'Cholera in 1970' (WER 1971;46, IRIS 10665/218451) states that cholera appeared 'in Guinea in West Africa' and that 'From Guinea, following the expected pattern the disease spread to 10 countries in West Africa and by the end of 1970 had infected Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Mali, Togo, DAHOMEY, Upper Volta, Nigeria and Niger' - Dahomey being the colonial-era name of Benin. Benin's infection is therefore explicitly downstream of Guinea's. (2) WER 1991;66(42) 'Cholera in Africa' (metadata Index 38) fixes Guinea's date and the sequence: 'In AUGUST 1970, Guinea was hit by a cholera outbreak, which was to spread rapidly to an entire continent that had been FREE OF THIS SCOURGE SINCE THE END OF THE NINETEENTH CENTURY. From Conakry, the disease first surged out eastwards along the coast (Map 1), reaching Sierra Leone, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Dahomey (now Benin), Nigeria and southern Cameroon successively BETWEEN SEPTEMBER 1970 AND FEBRUARY 1971.' The continent was free of cholera until August 1970 and Benin was reached no earlier than September. WHY THE ROW STOPS AT 31 JULY AND NOT 31 AUGUST: the September-to-February statement would justify closing the window on 31 August, but it is a retrospective written twenty years later with a two-month grain, so the row uses the unimpeachable bound instead - West Africa as a whole had no cholera before August 1970. The month of August 1970 is deliberately left empty rather than claimed either way. WHY THE FIRST-NOTIFICATION DATE COULD NOT BE USED: the WER 1970 annual article's Table 1 is titled 'Cases of Cholera Notified in 1970, by Date of First Notification and Country' and would settle this to the day, but the IRIS text layer for this 1971 scan has lost the table's column structure - the sixteen African country names run together as a single block and the date and total columns collapse into an unaligned token stream ('1311 1.9 39 20.10 610 23.8 2411 2712 2712 23.9 5.12 24.11 30 9 17.12'), fourteen date-like tokens for sixteen countries, so no token can be safely assigned to Dahomey. A future agent with the page image could read Dahomey's exact first-notification date off it and tighten this row. SURVEILLANCE STATUS: operational. Cholera was a quarantinable disease under the International Health Regulations throughout 1970 with mandatory immediate notification to WHO, and WHO was publishing the first-notification date for every newly infected country in the world that year - the notification system was not merely working but was the primary global instrument of the response. DOUBLE-COUNTING: national row and the primary count for the period; it contributes zero. Do not sum with the baseline's annual 1970 row of 175 cases, which covers the whole calendar year and therefore includes this window; the correct reading is that all 175 cases fell after this row's end date.

CONFLICT NOTED, NOT AVERAGED: the WHO revised annual series carried in the JHU baseline (cholera_data_jhu.csv, WHO Annual Cholera Report UID 302) gives Benin 175 cases / 37 deaths for 1970 - a later upward revision once delayed returns arrived. This row records the contemporaneous WER notification figure and its exact 16-day window; it is the sub-annual placement, not the annual magnitude, that is the contribution.
